name: Researching the Corruption
summary: Gershala Nightwhisper in Auberdine seeks corrupted brain stems from the creatures infesting Blackfathom Deeps. Disturbed by reports of the blood elves dabbling in demonic magic across the sea, he hopes to study the physiological descent of the naga and satyr to foresee—and perhaps avert—another catastrophic elven mutation.

sections.title: A Warning from History
sections.body: To the night elves of Kalimdor, the ruin of their ancient kin is a living memory etched into monsters. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne succumbed to the allure of demonic energies, warping themselves into horned satyrs or drowning into serpentine naga. Watching the high elves rebrand themselves as blood elves and embrace dark magic strikes Gershala Nightwhisper not as a distant curiosity, but as history doomed to repeat itself.

sections.title: Into the Deeps
sections.body: Blackfathom Deeps serves as an ideal specimen ground for Gershala's grim inquiry. Hidden beneath the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale, the subterranean temple ruins crawl with both satyr cultists and coiled naga. By sending an adventurer to harvest brain stems from both monstrosities, he hopes to dissect the biological link between arcane addiction, demonic corruption, and catastrophic bodily transformation.

sections.title: A Desperate Cure
sections.body: While Gershala's methods are chillingly anatomical, his stated intent is preventative. He believes that deciphering the exact physiological mutations shared by satyrs and naga could yield the knowledge needed to pull the blood elves back from total damnation. Whether any research conducted in darkshore can truly sway the desperate elves of Quel'Thalas remains an open question.

faq.q: Why does Gershala Nightwhisper care about the blood elves?
faq.answer: Gershala fears that the blood elves' flirtation with demonic powers will spawn another race of twisted monsters to menace Azeroth, just as past elven hubris gave rise to the satyrs and naga.

faq.q: Where do you gather the corrupted brain stems?
faq.answer: They are collected from the satyrs and naga dwelling within Blackfathom Deeps, an ancient temple complex buried along the Zoram Strand on the northwest coast of Ashenvale.

faq.q: Why does he specifically want satyr and naga samples?
faq.answer: Both the satyrs and the naga originated from elves who were warped by unnatural forces—satyrs through demonic bargains, and naga through the Sundering. Gershala wants to compare their brain mutations to map how elven physiology deteriorates under dark power.

faq.q: Who leads you to this task?
faq.answer: You can be directed to Gershala Nightwhisper in Auberdine via an introductory breadcrumb quest, 'The Corruption Abroad,' though he will also offer this investigation directly.

faq.q: What does Gershala plan to do with the specimens?
faq.answer: He plans to study the physiological correlations between the two forms of corruption, hoping the resulting knowledge could help forestall the blood elves' descent into deeper monstrosity.

faq.q: Is Auberdine directly threatened by Blackfathom Deeps?
faq.answer: While Blackfathom Deeps lies just across the southern border in Ashenvale, the night elves of Auberdine monitor the entire coastal region for signs of escalating demonic and Twilight corruption.

angles.text: For night elves, this research touches on the rawest wound in their history: the catastrophic degradation of their kin into the satyrs and naga who plague Kalimdor.
Druids hold an innate revulsion toward the satyrs, whose fel corruption defiles the natural dream and warps the land itself.
Gershala's grim investigation is a stark reminder of the physical and spiritual costs of reckless, unchecked magical dependence.
The Alliance keeps a wary eye on reports of the blood elves' descent into dark arts across the sea, dreading the emergence of a new demonic threat.
